texts: good. the scattering, Bevin Coombe, the Stilllight Lantern, the evening of day 495 of Year 2, and the 'fresh' and 'ground' properties handed to each feather are all carried.
good. 'that night' correctly copies day 495 of Year 2 forward, and the lantern's lit state is recorded both as a dated state and as a plain past fact.
good. the steady burning is anchored to the same night and correctly ordered before the Council's session the next afternoon.

mixed: the seeing, the pale shape and the shape's nearness to the water all come through, but 'of the Sunken Cove' was read as containment — the parse asserts the water sits inside the cove, which your wording does not state. If containment is what you mean, say it outright: 'Bevin Coombe saw a pale shape near the water in the Sunken Cove.'

bad: the 'before' clause is asserted as fact — the parse records at full strength a reaching event in which the shape did reach the Stilllight Lantern, the opposite of what your sentence says. State the non-occurrence directly instead: 'The shape turned away and never reached the Stilllight Lantern.'
good. 'the sighting' correctly resolves to Bevin Coombe's own seeing rather than minting a new one, and the Council is recorded as the recipient of the report.
good. 'the next afternoon' resolves to day 496 of Year 2 and is ordered after the previous night, and the emergency session is recorded as a kind of session.

bad: 'the report' — the thing actually logged — gets no slot on the logging event; it appears only inside the recorded classification, so 'what did the Council log?' returns the near-miss judgement rather than the report. The hedged 'as a possible …' phrase has no licensed slot of its own either. Split the logging from the judgement: 'The Council logged the report and judged that the report might be a wraith near-miss.'
good. the doubled feather ration, the Stilllight Station and the two-month duration all ride one keeping event.

bad: 'stay' is dropped — the parse records the keepers simply being alert, not continuing to be, so a standing watch order reads as a one-off state. A finite clause gives the continuation somewhere to live: 'The Council told the keepers of the West Row that they must stay alert.'

bad: 'sighting' is turned back into the verb 'see', so the denial lands on a seeing event rather than on sightings, and the quantifier 'no' leaves no record distinguishing it from a plain 'not'. Use a plain verb and a plain negation: 'The shape did not return.'
good. the judgement is recorded as the Council's opinion rather than as fact, the feather warding is typed outside that opinion, and the past-perfect 'had prevented' is kept inside it.
